# @stacklatte/chart-web

> React trading chart for plain web apps — HTML5 Canvas 2D, no WebAssembly, no `react-native-web`. Candlesticks, line charts, SMA/EMA/Bollinger Bands overlays, RSI/MACD/volume sub-panels, trade markers (entry/exit/stop-loss/take-profit), pointer/wheel pan-zoom, crosshair inspection, live-streaming updates, dark/light themes — MIT licensed. Same engine, same props, same LLM-safe `ChartConfig` as `@stacklatte/chart-core` (the React Native version).

## Install

```sh
npm install @stacklatte/chart-web
```

Only peers: `react >=19`, `react-dom >=19`. No native modules, no WASM runtime.

## Minimal usage

```tsx
import { SLChart } from '@stacklatte/chart-web';
import type { Candle } from '@stacklatte/chart-web';

<SLChart data={candles /* Candle[]: {timestamp, open, high, low, close} */} width={800} height={400} theme="dark" />
```

`width`/`height` are plain CSS-pixel numbers — measure your container with `ResizeObserver` or similar; there's no native `useWindowDimensions`.

## Generating config with an LLM

Prefer emitting a `ChartConfig` document over hand-written props when a model is generating chart setup — every string field is a closed enum (no raw hex colors, no arbitrary interval strings), and `buildChartPipeline` throws a structured, itemized error if the document doesn't validate instead of rendering something silently wrong.

```ts
import { buildChartPipeline } from '@stacklatte/chart-web';
const compiled = buildChartPipeline(config, candles); // -> spread into <SLChart {...compiled} width height />
```

The matching JSON Schema (draft-07, `additionalProperties: false` everywhere) is published at `../chart-core/dist/ChartConfig.schema.json` in the sibling `@stacklatte/chart-core` package (a dependency of this one) — use it directly as a structured-output / tool-call schema.
